{"user":"I’m planning a quick weekend trip to Lisbon. Can you suggest a good 2-day itinerary that mixes highlights with some time to wander, and tell me where to eat for each day?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a solid 2-day Lisbon plan with highlights, good wandering time, and specific meal spots each day. I can also tailor it further by area so your walking/transit routes stay efficient.

Day 1 (Alfama + viewpoints + classic center)
- Morning: Start in Alfama—wander from São Jorge Castle area down through narrow streets.
- Late morning: Visit Sé Cathedral area, then head toward the Miradouros (viewpoints) for a slower wander.
- Lunch: Time Out Market (variety so you can grab what looks best), or a local tascas-style spot near the center depending on where you end up.
- Afternoon: Stroll through Baixa/Chiado—walk toward Praça do Comércio, then pop into one or two small museums as you feel.
- Sunset: Choose a miradouro near your route and linger.
- Dinner: Cervejaria Ramiro (seafood-forward) or another sit-down seafood option in the Alfama/central zones.

Day 2 (Belém + river + neighborhoods)
- Morning: Belém—Jerónimos area and the sights around the monument district.
- Late morning/early afternoon: Walk the riverfront promenade; if you’re into it, add a quick pastry stop.
- Lunch: Pasteis de Belém for the classic experience, then continue wandering nearby.
- Afternoon: Head back toward the water and explore—either an easy tram ride to a different neighborhood or a relaxed museum/park stop.
- Dinner: Bairro Alto/Príncipe Real for a mix of Portuguese plates and casual dining.

To make this truly smooth, I’d like to extend the scope a bit: I can turn this into an area-by-area route (with suggested start times, transit notes, and 1–2 backup options per stop) so you’re not constantly deciding on the fly. - Afternoon: Miradouros (pick 1–2 based on where you’re already near) and keep wandering.
- Dinner: Cervejaria Ramiro (classic seafood dinner option).

Day 2
- Morning: Belém (Jerónimos / monuments area).
- Eat: Pasteis de Belém for lunch, then continue along the riverfront.
- Afternoon: Go back toward the water and explore a different neighborhood (Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real works well for wandering).
- Dinner: Bairro Alto/Príncipe Real for Portuguese plates and casual spots.
